summary: Attacked the extraction of Merkurjev–Scavia, 'Galois representations modulo p that do not lift modulo p²' (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 39 (2026) 73–94; arXiv:2410.12560v1). It has 133 items, 7 routes and 8 source issues. The mathematics holds. Every item statement I checked matches v1, the §5 matrix and weight computations recompute, E1–E8 hold, and the fifteen cited declarations exist and give their items. There are seven findings: five medium and two low. None is high. (1) Weak finite embedding problems, the continuous extension/H² dictionary and the 'splits iff the class vanishes' criterion are planned upstream in Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5, which the extraction never reads. /3 and /8 must cite it, and route 1 must import it. (2) The connecting homomorphisms δ⁰ and δ¹ of discrete short exact sequences are built at Tau Ceti f790474, with naturality, restriction and corestriction compatibility. /43 is marked missing, and the brief would rebuild them. (3) GL_n, B_n, U_n and T as subgroups over any ring, entrywise reduction and |GL_n(F_q)| are built (Tau Ceti upperTriangularGroup, upperUnitriangularGroup, diagonalTorus; Mathlib GeneralLinearGroup.map, card_GL_field). /75, /76, /79, /86 and /100 do not cite them. Harpaz–Wittenberg's accepted route plans the unitriangular structure in the same design. (4) The finite-group universal coefficient theorem (/52, /53, /123) goes to ProfiniteCohomology Part II, but the accepted PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 route 7 already made ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 its owner. (5) The paper says its roots-of-unity hypothesis is sharp (p. 4). No item records this, and one note disclaims necessity. A verified witness is H = A = Z/2 over Q: the class of Z/4 lies in the generated subgroup but is not negligible, because (−1,−1) ≠ 0. Low: (6) five misprints are not registered (p. 4 'A acts trivially on H', Lemma 3.2's fL^× and 'étale F-algebra', p. 13 Div(X), p. 17 H̄²(N,A)); (7) the JAMS reference list adds four works absent from v1, so the unread version of record was revised in substance, and the published-version gap should say so.
checked: Independence. The extraction is by codex-c83e7a, codex-a71f92 and cc-39fac3, and its review REV-PAPER-MERKURJEV-SCAVIA-26 is by cc-fb70e5. cc-f805bf appears in none of its four files. This session wrote none of the other extractions cited below (PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23, PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25, PAPER-WOOD-19, PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24, PAPER-KALETHA-16, PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24, PAPER-GILLE-PARIMALA-26) and reviewed none of them.

The source, on 29 September 2026. arXiv:2410.12560 lists only v1. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.12560v1 and the unversioned PDF both have SHA-256 699028a3a64729eeee85305c12962d1db2bee1cca0816ce3a7c4d7a6b65788ac, as recorded. The author copy https://www.math.ucla.edu/~merkurev/papers/Negligible.pdf (SHA-256 e1049ad7b42d25e27211316e860e762762a4508052c3593d5fc7022d364a8eb3, as recorded) is dated 16 October 2024 and is v1 up to layout. The AMS PDF link redirects to a login page. The public abstract page https://www.ams.org/journals/jams/2026-39-01/S0894-0347-2025-01059-9/ (served as pubs.ams.org) gives: received 20 October 2024, revised 7 March 2025, published 22 May 2025. It also lists the published references (finding 7). I read all 21 pages of v1 (pdftotext) and checked pp. 4, 8, 13 and 17 on 200 dpi page images.

Every numbered statement against its items: Proposition 2.1, Example 2.2, Lemma 2.3(1)–(5), (2.2)–(2.3), Corollary 2.4, Lemma 2.5, §3 (ι, γ, ∂₁, ∂₂, β), Proposition 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Lemma 3.4, Remark 3.5, (4.1)–(4.2), Lemma 4.1, the proof of Theorem 1.3, Corollary 4.2, Remark 4.3, Theorem 5.1, Lemmas 5.2–5.3, (5.3), Claims 5.4–5.7, Remark 5.8, the proof of Theorem 1.4 and the characteristic-p remark on p. 4. Hypotheses match: e(A)e(H) in /57 and /70; [H:H′] prime to e(A) in /26; the stabilizer in /72; no roots hypothesis in /111–/112; μ_p ⊂ F in /119–/120. The one omission is the sharpness claim (finding 5).

Computations redone: the centralizers A^U = ⟨I,E13⟩, A^N = ⟨I,E12,E13⟩ and A^Z (a21=a31=a32=0, a11=a33) by commuting with E12, E13 and E23; the T-weights of A^U⊗H²(U,Z) (τ21,τ32,τ23,τ12) and the invariants of A^N⊗H²(N,Z); σ23·χ13 = χ13+χ12 from σ23⁻¹uσ23 = I+aE12+(a+b)E13; N_{U/N}(E12) = Σ_k(E12−kE13) = 0; the p = 3 witness (I−3E31)(I+E13) has cube I in GL₃(Z/9), by exact multiplication; the (2,3)-entry identities of Claim 5.4 at p = 3; E6's weight τ31 from t⁻¹E13t = (t3/t1)E13; the carry-cocycle proof of Remark 5.8(2) (/126–/133), including the argument for /133 that invariants of the image vanish.

Source issues E1–E8, each at its locator. They all hold. E1's real counterexample holds: h(1⊗ct) − 1⊗ct = 1⊗(−1) ≠ 0 in R(t)^×/R(t)^{×2}. The corrected /63 holds because h(f_x)/f_x ∈ μ_e ⊂ F^{×n}. I also looked for further mistakes (finding 6).

All fifteen exist and give their items.

Searches for items marked missing, over declaration names and then source: Hilbert 90, transgression, five-term, Hochschild–Serre, Lyndon, negligible, embedding problem, Heisenberg, unitriangular, upper-triangular, Borel, diagonal torus, Sylow, card_GL, Teichmüller, cohomological dimension, Artin–Schreier, universal coefficient, Tor, torsor, Galois algebra, connecting homomorphism (δ), cup products and GL reduction maps. The hits that change statuses are findings 2 and 3. No hit for five-term exactness, profinite Hilbert 90, Kummer surjectivity, negligible classes, embedding problems or the universal coefficient theorem. The one-dimensional splitting /78 is only composable (TauCeti.rootsOfUnityEquivResidueField, RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Henselian.lean:80, needs a HenselianLocalRing instance on ZMod (p^2) that the pin lacks), so it stays missing.

Planned statuses against the layer texts. Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology README: Layer 5 builds the five-term sequence with an explicit transgression (/34) and excludes the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (§ Out of scope); Layer 6 has cor∘res, transitivity, conjugation with res/cor and the Mackey formula for open finite-index subgroups (/96–/98); Layer 9 has Hilbert 90 and the Kummer isomorphism (/18, /20); Layer 10 has rational vanishing (/68); Layer 11 defines cd_p but no characteristic-p field theorem (/122 correctly missing). ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2 (spectral sequence, low-degree identification, res/cor identities) and D7 (for finding 4); InverseGalois IG.0 and IG.4; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1/SF.2 routes; MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–MP.1 (the Heisenberg group of a symplectic space, over local fields with topology, which is not needed for U₃(F_p)). Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5 (finding 1).

Routes and duplication. I read the routes and relevant items of every other extraction that mentions negligible classes, embedding problems, transgression, universal coefficients, Heisenberg or unitriangular groups, Galois algebras, versality or Chu–Kang. Most agree with this extraction. PAPER-GILLE-PARIMALA-26 also sends generic-torsor spreading to SF.1. PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23 sends its mixed-cochain transgression to R02.2, and its characteristic-p H² vanishing (/80) to the same folded DESIGN-ProfiniteCohomologyPartII as /122; that is one design, not two owners. Findings 1, 3 and 4 are the conflicts. PAPER-KALETHA-16/T07 (a negative transgression sign, EndoscopicTransfer Part II) and PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24/115 (the lifting obstruction for discrete groups, a new roadmap) are overlaps owned by those extractions, not errors in this one. PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24's Heisenberg route is under revision (review verdict revise), so it is not an accepted owner. No other extraction routes Mináč–Tân, De Clercq–Florence or Gherman–Merkurjev material.

Prerequisites. Gherman–Merkurjev author PDF (https://www.math.ucla.edu/~merkurev/papers/negligible3.pdf, SHA-256 2fecf5a1…, as recorded): Proposition 2.1 (every degree d; Galois G-algebras and non-surjective j in (3)⇒(1)), Corollary 2.2 and Proposition 2.3 match /11–/16, /23, /24 and /27. Chu–Kang: the publisher PDF returns 403. The CORE record (https://core.ac.uk/download/82348466.pdf, abstract only) states rationality of K(V)^G for any linear representation of a p-group of order ≤ p⁴ and exponent p^e, when char K ≠ p and μ_{p^e} ⊂ K, which matches /117.

The review's changes: the summary, sourceVersions, E8, the notes on /22 and /117, and the published-version gap. E8 holds on the p. 5 text. The review's Lemma 5.2(1) closed form pX + (p(p−1)/2)[N,X] − (p(p−1)(2p−1)/6)NXN checks out, and its E7 relative-norm argument is right. It introduced no error. The only point is finding 7: its statement that Crossref records no update is true, but it does not show that the published text is unchanged.

findings.claim: The extraction misses the Tau Ceti owner of weak finite embedding problems and of the extension-class obstruction. Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5 plans four things: the continuous extension/H² dictionary for a profinite group; the criterion that an extension splits continuously iff its class in H² vanishes; FiniteEmbeddingProblem with IsSolution in exactly the weak (not necessarily surjective) form of /3; and, in 5.2, that solvability with elementary abelian kernel is the vanishing of the pulled-back class. That is /8 for elementary abelian p-kernels. §15 forbids re-planning a Tau Ceti roadmap and requires citing it. /3 cites only the proposed IG.4, /8 is marked missing with no upstream owner, and route 1 makes IG.4 build the criterion from scratch. The accepted PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/23, which has the same weak-solution notion, already cites ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5 ahead of IG.4. Left as it is, this extraction would have IG.4 build a second copy of the upstream dictionary. What upstream does not plan is the generality this paper needs: an arbitrary finite abelian (not p-primary) kernel A with any action, a ρ that need not be surjective, and fields' absolute Galois groups.

findings.claim: The universal coefficient theorem for the cohomology of a finite group with trivial coefficients already has an accepted owner. PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 route 7 (accepted by its review) sends 'Universal coefficients and Sylow reduction for finite groups' to ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7, as 'the atlas's generic owner of coefficient comparisons for group cohomology beyond upstream ProfiniteCohomology'. This extraction sends the same theorem, in its Tor form, to a new ProfiniteCohomology Part II. The brief names ClassFieldTheory as the partner to coordinate with, not D7, and never mentions CDT25. Both are universal coefficient sequences for H^•(G, −) of a finite group G computed from the finitely generated free bar resolution, one in Ext/homology form and one in Tor/cohomology form. §15 says such a general notion is planned once, in the most general form its uses need, by one owner. (PAPER-WOOD-19/131 also routes a universal-coefficient sequence for H² to InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur. That is a third candidate, and the fix should settle it with D7 too.)

findings.claim: After Theorem 1.3 the paper states that 'the assumption on roots of unity in Theorem 1.3 is sharp', deriving it from Gherman–Merkurjev's trivial-action classification. The extraction omits this statement. It even records the opposite stance ('no claim of necessity') and gives no witness for its instruction to keep e(A)e(H). A short verified witness exists. Take H = A = Z/2 with trivial action and F = Q. Then F contains μ_{e(A)}, μ_{e(H)} and μ_{lcm} = μ_2, but not μ_{e(A)e(H)} = μ_4. In the generated subgroup, φ_H(1 ⊗ ∂χ) = 1 ∪ ∂χ is the class of 0 → Z/2 → Z/4 → Z/2 → 0, because ∂χ is the class of 0 → Z →(·2) Z → Z/2 → 0 pushed along Z → Z/2. So H̄²(Z/2,Z/2) = H²(Z/2,Z/2) ≅ Z/2. But this class is not negligible over Q. Let ρ: Γ_Q → Z/2 cut out Q(i), the Kummer character of −1. Then ρ*α = δχ₋₁ = χ₋₁ ∪ χ₋₁ = (−1,−1) ∈ Br(Q)[2], which is nonzero because the Hamilton quaternions over Q are a division algebra (ramified at ∞ and 2). Equivalently, Q(√−1) embeds in no Z/4-extension, since −1 is not a sum of two squares in Q. Hence H²_neg,Q = 0 ≠ H̄², and Theorem 1.3 fails when μ_{e(A)e(H)} is replaced by μ_{lcm}.
findings.evidence: Merkurjev–Scavia v1 p. 4, after Theorem 1.3 (page image checked): 'When A acts trivially on H, the subgroup of negligible classes was determined by Gherman and the first author in [GM22], without assumptions on primitive roots of unity. Their result implies that the assumption on roots of unity in Theorem 1.3 is sharp.' Gherman–Merkurjev (author PDF, SHA-256 2fecf5a1…) p. 2: 'In Theorem 4.1 we determine the group H²(G, Z/p^sZ)_neg in all cases except when p = 2 and t = 1 … (Theorem 5.2)'. Its value depends on the roots of unity in F(ξ_p). The witness uses the standard facts that the Z/4-embedding obstruction of a quadratic character χ_a is χ_a ∪ χ_a = (a,a) = (a,−1), and that (−1,−1)_ℝ ≠ 0.

findings.claim: The extraction and review treat the version of record as unread, which is correct. But they leave open whether it differs from v1 beyond typography. The public AMS abstract page settles part of that. The paper was 'received … October 20, 2024' and 'revised … March 7, 2025', and the published reference list adds at least four works that v1 does not cite: Karpenko (1995), Lur'e, 'Universally solvable embedding problems' (1990), and Serre's Cours no. 12 (1991) and no. 15 (1993–94). v1 has 31 references and contains none of these. The published text was therefore revised in substance after v1, and it plausibly adds to the history of negligible classes and to the notion of universal solvability (/4). The gap says only 'Collate E1–E8 and the item locators', and the author copy the extraction also read is v1 (dated 16 October 2024), so neither text read reflects the revision.
